newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-First Enterprise sees 35 branches in '96.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-First Enterprise sees 35 branches in '96.

text.p: First Enterprise Financial Group Inc, a specialty finance company, expects its network of branch offices to expand to 35 by year-end, said Michael Harrington, president and chief executive officer.
At June 30, the Evanston, Ill.-based company that became publicly traded on July 26 operated 29 branches.
"Our growth is on track, and we expect to add 12 to 16 new locations a year at least over the next five years," Harrington said in a telephone interview.

Harrington said the company is decentralized by having offices in eight southern states, where a physical presence gives it a competitive edge. Illinois is targeted for the company's expansion, but the timetable is yet to be set.
Operating under the name of First Enterprise Acceptance Co, the company buys and services installment sales contracts from dealers for financing the sale of used cars, vans and light trucks.
Its niche market is the car buyer with a limited access to traditional sources of credit because of low incomes or past credit problems.

The seasonality of the industry cut into the company's third-quarter volume of contracts purchased, but Harrington said this was a normal phenomenon since used car sales generally wane during the summer. He said the market, because of affordability and the quality of vehicles coming off lease, remains strong. "We expect to return to higher levels of volume in the fourth quarter," he noted.
Outstanding contract purchase agreements with dealers grew to 1,025 at June 30 from 508 a year earlier.
The executive also said, "We anticipate an excellent level of profitability for the full year."
Harrington said he agrees with the $0.86 per share earnings consensus for 1996. "I'm very comfortable with the projections investment bankers have made," he said.
For the six months ended June 30, First Enterprise posted pro forma earnings of $0.41 a share on revenue of $12.2 million.

Dain Bosworth analyst Jay Tejera told Reuters he initiated coverage of First Enterprise last week with a buy rating on the stock. For 1997, he projects its earnings will rise to about $1.25 per share.
"We like their decentralized, conservative strategy," Tejera said.
First Enterprise shares closed off 1/8 at 10.
